stage_designation.quote: The overall design parameters for stage 8E-8 are listed in table I ... The blade geometry for rotor 8E is presented in table IV and that for stator 8 is presented in table V.

same_stage_as_reference_5.value: the test stage is the one described in NASA TM X-2926 (Osborn, Urasek, Moore 1973, blade-tip solidity 1.5)
same_stage_as_reference_5.quote: The test stage is the same one that was described in detail in reference 5. Thus only a brief description is included herein for completeness.

design_pressure_ratio_text.quote: This stage was designed for an overall pressure ratio of 1.750 at a flow of 29.5 kilograms per second (200.6 kg sec/m2 of annulus area).

design_weight_flow_text.quote: at a flow of 29.5 kilograms per second (200.6 kg sec/m2 of annulus area)

design_tip_speed_text.quote: The design tip speed was 423 meters per second.

fan_diameter_hub_tip.quote: The hub-tip radius ratio of the 50-centimeter-diameter fan was 0.5.

rotor_tip_solidity.quote: The stage was designed for a tip solidity of 1.5 for the rotor and 1.5 for the stator.

stator_tip_solidity.quote: The stage was designed for a tip solidity of 1.5 for the rotor and 1.5 for the stator.

rotor_blade_count.quote: This resulted in 49 rotor blades with an aspect ratio of 2.4 and 54 stator blades with an aspect ratio of 2.0.

rotor_aspect_ratio.quote: 49 rotor blades with an aspect ratio of 2.4

stator_blade_count.quote: 54 stator blades with an aspect ratio of 2.0.

stator_aspect_ratio.quote: 54 stator blades with an aspect ratio of 2.0.

rotor_part_span_damper.value: about 48 percent of span from the outlet rotor tip; max damper thickness 0.214 cm
rotor_part_span_damper.quote: The rotor had a part-span damper located at about 48 percent of span from the outlet rotor tip. The maximum thickness of the damper was 0.214 centimeter.

rotor_hub_te_to_stator_hub_le.quote: The axial spacing between the rotor-hub trailing edge and the stator-hub leading edge was 3.33 centimeters.

profile_type.value: not stated in TP-2049 (refers to TM X-2926); X FACTOR < 1 and separate ZTC/KTC columns in Tables IV-V imply multiple-circular-arc sections for both rotor 8E and stator 8

tip_clearances_nonrotating.quote: (a) Nominal nonrotating rotor tip clearance, 0.061 cm ... (c) ... 0.140 cm ... (d) ... 0.178 cm (Table VI); TABLE VII/VIII/IX/X ... ROTOR TIP CLEARANCE OF 0.061 / 0.102 / 0.140 / 0.178 cm; in-text table: 0.061, .102, .140, .178

baseline_clearance.quote: The insert was machined so that it was parallel to the rotor tip with a nominal (nonrotating) clearance of 0.061 centimeter.

clearance_change_method.value: uniform increment of material removed from a casing insert over the rotor tips, faired to the casing about 1.3 cm upstream of the LE and downstream of the TE
clearance_change_method.quote: For the tip clearance studies a uniform increment of material was removed from the insert (fig. 5) in the region over the rotor tip. The diameter was then faired to the casing diameter to approximately 1.3 centimeters upstream of the blade leading edge and downstream of the trailing edge.

running_clearance_correction.unit: cm (running clearance is this much less than the nonrotating values at design speed)
running_clearance_correction.quote: The dynamic growth of the wheel and blades plus the eccentricity was calculated to be approximately 0.040 centimeter at design speed; and thus the running clearances at design speed were approximately 0.040 centimeter less than the values presented.

running_clearance_fraction.value: 0.2 to 1.2 percent of leading-edge blade height
running_clearance_fraction.quote: Thus the calculated running clearance will be 0.2 to 1.2 percent of leading-edge blade height.

stall_margin_by_clearance.quote: The stall margins based on an assumed operating line passing through the stall point at a clearance of 0.178 centimeter, at design speed, are as follows: (table)

data_tables_per_clearance.value: Table VII 0.061 cm, Table VIII 0.102 cm, Table IX 0.140 cm, Table X 0.178 cm (rotor 8E then stator 8); Table VI (a)-(d) overall
data_tables_per_clearance.quote: The blade-element data for the four rotor tip clearances are presented for the rotor and stator in tables VII to X.

test_speeds.value: 70 and 100 percent for every clearance; at 0.061 cm also near-stall at 50, 60, 80, 90 percent
test_speeds.quote: For each clearance, data were obtained over the stable operating range at 70 and 100 percent of design speed. At the smallest clearance, near-stall conditions were also surveyed at 50, 60, 80, and 90 percent of design speed.

survey_stations.value: 1 upstream of rotor Z = -2.540, 2 between rotor and stator Z = 6.096, 3 downstream of stator Z = 13.462 cm (Fig. 2 footnote a); 11 radial positions
survey_stations.quote: aInstrumentation survey plane (Fig. 2); Data were recorded at 11 radial positions for each speed and flow condition.

stator_passage_traverse.quote: The combination probe downstream of the stator (station 3) was circumferentially traversed one stator blade passage (6.7°) counterclockwise from the nominal value shown.

data_translated_to_blade_edges.quote: The data, measured at the three measuring stations, were translated to the rotor and stator blade leading and trailing edges along design streamlines by the method presented in reference 4.

zic_definition.quote: ZIC axial distance from inlet hub to blade leading edge, cm

percent_span_definition.quote: PERCENT SPAN percent of blade span from tip at rotor outlet
